provenance.name: E. coli SOS DNA Repair Network (Gardner et al., Science 2003)
provenance.technology: Custom dual-dye cDNA glass slide microarrays with steady-state plasmid overexpression
provenance.data_type: Normalized steady-state log expression ratios relative to unperturbed wild-type control
provenance.perturbation_type: Transcriptional plasmid overexpression of individual genes (9 single-gene perturbations)
citations: Gardner, T. S., di Bernardo, D., Lorenz, D., & Collins, J. J. (2003). Inferring genetic networks and identifying compound mode of action via expression profiling. Science, 301(5629), 102-105. DOI: 10.1126/science.1081900
Wildenhain, J. (2004). In Silico Modelling of Gene Networks and Reverse Engineering of Transcriptional Networks. Bachelor of Honours Thesis, University of Edinburgh.

Wildenhain, J., & Crampin, E. J. (2006). Reconstructing gene regulatory networks: from random to scale-free connectivity. IEE Proceedings - Systems Biology, 153(4), 247-256. DOI: 10.1049/ip-syb:20050073
provenance.overview: The SOS response is the canonical bacterial DNA repair network in E. coli. When DNA suffers damage (UV irradiation, chemical cross-linking, mitomycin C), single-stranded DNA activates RecA to stimulate the autocatalytic cleavage of the master repressor LexA, derepressing over 40 SOS genes.

genes_annotated.recA: Recombinase A; forms nucleoprotein filament on ssDNA; coprotease stimulating LexA and UmuD cleavage.
genes_annotated.lexA: Master transcriptional repressor of the SOS regulon; binds palindromic SOS boxes to repress repair genes.
genes_annotated.ssb: Single-stranded DNA-binding protein; binds and protects single-stranded DNA replication intermediates.
genes_annotated.recF: Recombination factor F; loads RecA protein onto single-stranded DNA gaps alongside RecO and RecR.
genes_annotated.dinI: DNA damage-inducible protein I; binds RecA nucleoprotein filaments to modulate coprotease activity.
genes_annotated.umuDC: DNA polymerase V complex subunits (UmuD'2C); error-prone translesion DNA synthesis past bulky adducts.
genes_annotated.rpoD: RNA polymerase sigma 70 factor; master housekeeping transcription initiation factor.
genes_annotated.rpoH: RNA polymerase sigma 32 factor; directs transcription of cytoplasmic heat-shock chaperones and proteases.
genes_annotated.rpoS: RNA polymerase sigma 38 factor; master regulator of stationary-phase and general environmental stress response.

provenance.wrangling_procedure:
1. Raw Cy3/Cy5 fluorescence intensities measured across 4 technical replicates per experiment.
2. Background correction and LOWESS intensity-dependent normalization applied.
3. Steady-state expression ratios X_ij = r_ij computed as log2(perturbed / control).
4. Perturbation matrix U defined with known plasmid induction levels on the diagonal.

how_raw_data_is_used.wrangled_direct: Algorithms consume the 9x9 expression ratio matrix X and perturbation matrix U directly. Stepwise AIC regression (S2G/G2S), NIR multiple regression, FAST SVD pseudo-inversion, and Neural ODEs solve A * X = -U to derive the continuous Jacobian without running an ODE simulation.
how_raw_data_is_used.biophysical_fit: The real steady states are used to estimate biophysical parameters: basal production rates v_i = b_i * x_i^ctrl, degradation constants b_i = 1.0, and Hill threshold affinities K_ij = median(|X_j|) + 0.1. These parameters are passed to the non-linear Hill ODE solver (dx_i/dt = v_i * Prod(Hill) - b_i * x_i + u_i) to simulate continuous transient relaxation trajectories x_i(t) and limit-cycle stability.
